name: CR-Int-17-misc-06
questiontext:
By taking logarithms to the base \(e\) establish that \(a^x\) can be written as \(e^{xlna}\). Hence find \[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Using the laws of logarithms \[e^{ln(x)} = x\] and \[ln(x^k) = kln(x)\] we get that

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 a^x &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  e^{ln(a^x)} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  e^{x\cdot ln(a)}
 \end{array}\]

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int e^{x\cdot ln(a)} d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}}
 \end{array}\]
